canonical_evidence.scene_contract: Hiraṇyākṣa sees Varaha rising from the water with Earth; no body-form or limb-count specification.
Varaha bears Earth on the tusk and lowers her into the water; no arm-count specification.
The asura is mace-bearing and Varaha takes a raised mace for their duel; establishes the scene-specific mace action, not total arm count.
Varaha manifests/holds the great discus in his hand after his mace falls; specifies hand use, not total arm count.
Varaha strikes with the discus held in hand; specifies action, not total arm count.
Varaha strikes with his big toe near the asura’s ear; specifies the toe action, not a universal limb arrangement.

canonical_evidence.text: tvaci chando romasvapi kuśagaṇaścakṣuṣi ghṛtaṃ / caturhotāro’ṅghrau srugapi vadane codara iḍā / grahā jihvāyāṃ ... karṇe ca camasā / ... galadeśe’pyupasadaḥ
canonical_evidence.scene_contract: Maps yajna elements to skin, hair, eyes, feet, face, belly, tongue, ears, virility and neck; says nothing about arm count.

chapter_12.scope: D012 draft specifies natural quadruped boar anatomy for its own infant, growth, search and Earth-lifting scenes; D012 S003 explicitly requires four connected legs for the infant. This scene-specific anatomy is not a chapter-wide D013 rule.
chapter_12.shared_identity: divine Varaha with recognizable elongated boar snout, tusks and upright ears, matte earth-pigment palette
chapter_12.reference_visual_observation: Visually inspected exact D012-owned reference: one natural quadruped boar with elongated broad snout, upturned tusks, upright ears, reddish/deep-brown fur, orange/ochre crown, collar and cloth, on warm cream/ochre ground; matte drawn contours. It defines the shared identity and earth palette, while its quadruped pose is local to D012 scene contracts.

chapter_13.variant: Source-grounded functional variant: a hand-bearing combat posture in S004-S006 to carry the raised mace and wield the discus, followed by the explicit big-toe strike in S007. These are scene actions, not a source-given total arm count or universal humanoid form.
chapter_13.scope: Use hand-bearing weapon actions in S004-S006 and the toe action in S007 only. The source establishes no limb-count claim for S001-S003 or S008-S010; verse 13-9 maps yajna symbolism to body regions without prescribing arm count.
